THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,

THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard Sri Sanjay S.Katageri, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt.Girija S.Hiremath, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and Sri. Gouri Shankar Mot, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

The present petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer :-
"To quash the said criminal proceedings in Session Case No.5068/2022 as pending on the file of I Addl. District and Session Judge, Hubballi, on the basis of charge sheet filed by the Hubballi-  Dharwad Women Police Station in  C.C.No.8472/2021, arising out of Crime  No.61/2020, insofar as the petitioner herein are for the alleged offences punishable under Section 498A, 306 r/w Section 149 of IPC by allowing this criminal petition."
3.

entities.text: I Addl. District and Session Judge, Hubballi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Though the matter is listed for admission by consent of the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

4. The brief facts of the case are as under :-
A complaint came to be filed by the mother of the deceased by name Tasnima Kausar Shekh with Women Police Station, Hubballi-Dharwad on 01.02.2020, which was registered in Crime No.61/2020 for the offence punishable 498A, 306 r/w 149 IPC.
Gist of the complaint averments
reveal that 2 n d daughter of the complainant was married to one Sri Abdul Khadir Sutar on 02.05.2019.
At the time of marriage, a sum of Rs.75,000/- was given as dowry and Rs.4,00,000/- was spent for the marriage.

After the marriage, the daughter of the complainant joined the matrimonial home and at that juncture, petitioners and others started ill-treating her and they demanded additional dowry and were harassing the deceased physically and mentally.

Later on, the gold ornaments which are given at the time of marriage were also misappropriated by the husband and other members of the family and when this aspect of the matter was reported to the police by the deceased, they advised the husband of the deceased and others.

On 08.09.2020, complainant visited the Smt Chandbi W/O Usman Alias Abdulgani ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107503263/
3 matrimonial home and brought back the daughter as there was severe ill-treatment physically and mentally.

entities.text: Smt Chandbi W/O Usman Alias Abdulgani ... vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even when the deceased was staying with the parental house, the petitioner and others ill-treated her over mobile telephone and unable to bear the harassment, on 30.11.2020 at about 10.30 p.m., daughter of the complainant committed suicide by hanging herself to the ceiling fan.

Based on the complaint,
police registered the case and thoroughly investigated the matter and filed charge sheet.
Learned Magistrate took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and committed the matter to the District Judge for trial.
When the matter stood thus, present petition is filed U/sec.482 Cr.P.C. with the aforesaid prayer.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri Sanjay S.Katageri, learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the petitioners are no way responsible for the incident that has occurred in the parental house of the deceased and so far as petitioners No.4 and 5 are concerned, they are residing elsewhere in Maharashtra State and they had no direct or indirect nexus with the suicidal death of the daughter of the complainant and they have been falsely implicated in the case.

6. He further pointed out that the 3r d petitioner is a student aged 20 years at no stretch of imagination could be constituted she has also harassed the deceased and sought for allowing the petition.

7. Per contra, Sri learned High Court Government Pleader opposed the case of the petitioners by contending that after thorough investigation, the Investigation Officer has collected such necessary materials to proceed against all the petitioners and other accused persons and filed charge sheet and sought for dismissal of the petition.
8. Sri Gouri Shankar Mot, learned counsel representing the defacto complainant adopted the arguments of learned High Court Government Pleader.

He further contended that the material on record would also indicate that all the petitioners including petitioners No.3 to 5 have harassed the deceased over telephone even after she took the shelter in the parental house and unable to bear the harassment, left with no alternative, she committed suicide and since the death has occurred within seven years of marriage, prosecution enjoys the presumption as is contemplated U/sec.113-A and 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act and sought for dismissal of the petition.
9.
In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
10. On such perusal of the material on record, it is seen that the marriage of the deceased with Abdul Khadir Sutar on 02.05.2019 is not in dispute.
Admittedly, suicidal death has taken place in the parental house.
Mother of the deceased is the complainant.
On account of the serious matrimonial differences, deceased was brought to the parental house on 08.09.2020.
On 30.11.2020, deceased has hung herself with the ceiling fan by using her veil at about 10.30 p.m.

sentences.text: 4 11. Whether at all the petitioners are all responsible for the suicidal death of the deceased or not cannot be decided by this Court by holding a mini trial.
It is for the trial Court to form an opinion after full-fledged trial.

12. However having said thus, petitioners No.4 and 5 are residing elsewhere with their respective husbands' in Maharashtra State and they were not sharing the common roof even when the deceased was living with her husband and other relatives.

13. Taking note of these aspects of the matter and following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others V/s State of Bihar and others reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, this Court is of the considered opinion that omnibus allegations and those allegations held against petitioners No.4 and 5, this Court is of the considered opinion that continuation of the criminal proceedings as against petitioners No.4 and 5 are unwarranted.
Therefore, a case is made out to quash the proceedings as against petitioners No.4 and 5.
14.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others V/s State of Bihar and others reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But insofar as other petitioners are concerned, there are materials on record to proceed with the trial.
More so, when they are sharing common roof when the deceased was living in the matrimonial home.
15. The contention of the counsel for the petitioners that the 3 r d petitioner was only a student - 10 - aged 20 years as on the date of incident is no ground to quash the criminal proceedings.
16. Accordingly, the following order is passed.
ORDER Petition is allowed in part.
is hereby dismissed.

Petition prayer insofar as petitioners No.4 and 5 are allowed and pending criminal proceedings in S.C.No.5068/2022 on the file of I Addl.District and Sessions Judge, Hubballi are hereby quashed.
The observations made by this Court during the course of this order shall not affect the rights of the prosecution or the accused in the pending trial insofar as remaining accused persons are concerned.
